claim: In silico models of complexes formed by analogues of a cancer drug and its receptor may enable strategic redesign of existing drugs to overcome mutations that lead to drug resistance in prostate cancer.
source: By using in silico models of the complexes formed by analogues of a cancer drug and its receptor, it may be possible to strategically redesign existing drugs and win the race against mutations that lead to drug resistance in prostate cancer.
evidence: The claim is presented as a possibility based on computational modeling approaches, representing a speculative statement about potential drug design strategies.

claim: Mutations lead to drug resistance in prostate cancer.
source: By using in silico models of the complexes formed by analogues of a cancer drug and its receptor, it may be possible to strategically redesign existing drugs and win the race against mutations that lead to drug resistance in prostate cancer.
evidence: The statement assumes as background that mutations cause drug resistance in prostate cancer, which is presented as established context for the proposed solution.

claim: Designer antiandrogens are being developed to address drug resistance.
source: Designer antiandrogens join the race against drug resistance
evidence: The title implies that designer antiandrogens represent an approach being pursued to combat drug resistance, though this is stated metaphorically rather than explicitly.
